<explanation>
This project is a multi-module framework designed to extend MyBatis functionality – the “MyBatis-Plus” project. Its purpose is to simplify development by providing utilities such as code generation, conditional query wrappers, pagination, auto-configuration for Spring Boot, and other “plus” enhancements that sit on top of MyBatis. The project is organized into numerous modules (for example: mybatis-plus-annotation, mybatis-plus-core, mybatis-plus-extension, mybatis-plus-generator, mybatis-plus-jsqlparser-support, mybatis-plus-spring, and several Spring Boot starter modules) that together form a cohesive ecosystem which can be integrated into applications using MyBatis.

When designing your system design architecture diagram for this project, consider the following guidelines:

1. Identify the Main Components:
   • MyBatis-Plus Core: The heart of the framework which includes core functionality (e.g., SQL session factory builder, mapper registry, query/condition wrappers, handlers and toolkits).
   • Annotation Module: Contains annotations that mark database properties and configurations (such as @TableField, @TableId, etc.) to drive ORM behavior.
   • Extension Module: Provides additional features like plugins (e.g., pagination, optimistic locker, interceptor-based SQL modifications), advanced type handlers, dynamic table name features, and active record support.
   • Code Generator (mybatis-plus-generator): Automates the generation of entity classes, mapper interfaces, and XML mapping files. It is tightly coupled with the core but functions as its own utility module.
   • JSQLParser Support: Modules (including both JSQLParser-4.9 and JSQLParser-5.0 versions) that enable advanced SQL parsing and manipulation, caching support, and integration with MyBatis-Plus functions.
   • Spring Integration Components: Comprising the mybatis-plus-spring, spring-boot-starter (and its variations for Spring Boot 2 and 3) modules along with auto-configuration classes. These components allow seamless integration into Spring-based applications by providing auto-configuration, enhanced DI support, and configuration customization.
   • Test and Example Components: The project also contains a vast test suite and sample applications that illustrate how each module works and integrates.

2. Define Relationships and Interactions:
   • MyBatis-Plus Core is central. Most other modules such as the Annotation, Extension, Code Generator, and JSQLParser modules depend on and extend its functionalities.
   • The Extension module plugs into the Core to provide additional features. For example, its plugins and enhanced type handlers augment core SQL operations.
   • The Code Generator uses configurations defined in the Core and Annotation modules to build out mappings and generate code.
   • The Spring-specific modules (including auto-configuration and Spring Boot starter modules) wrap around the Core and Extension modules to ensure proper dependency injection, configuration, and integration with Spring’s lifecycle.
   • The JSQLParser support modules sit as specialized services, assisting with SQL parsing and caching; they enable better performance (and enhanced features like dynamic table name handling) by enriching the data processing pipeline.

3. Architectural Patterns and Design Principles:
   • Modular Design – The project is clearly divided into discrete modules that each focus on different concerns. This separation of concerns simplifies maintenance and extension.
   • Plugin and Extension Mechanism – Many of the modules (especially the Extension and JSQLParser ones) implement plugin-based designs that allow the framework to be highly extensible and customize behavior at runtime.
   • Auto-Configuration (for Spring Boot integration) – Many Spring modules leverage Spring Boot’s auto-configuration pattern, enabling minimal manual configuration.
   • Active Record Pattern – The framework supports a style where domain models are responsible for their own database operations.
   • Layered Architecture – At the bottom, you have low-level database connection and MyBatis functions; on top layer, the framework activities (wrappers, interceptors, and auto configuration) build a more feature-rich toolkit.

4. Relevant Technologies and Frameworks:
   • MyBatis (as the underlying ORM)
   • Spring/Spring Boot for auto-configuration and integration
   • Gradle (the build system as seen from the build.gradle files)
   • JSQLParser (both versions for SQL parsing support)
   • Java and Kotlin (source directories indicate support for both languages)
   • Testing frameworks (JUnit, etc.) indicated by the extensive test suite

5. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram:
   • Use a component or module diagram format which clearly separates each module as distinct, labeled blocks.
   • Emphasize the core at the center with directional arrows illustrating dependency flows to the Annotation, Extension, Code Generator, and JSQLParser modules.
   • For the Spring Boot integration, show how the auto-configuration components wrap around the Core and Extension modules to provide dependency injection and configuration management.
   • Make clear annotation of optional integrations (for example, Spring Boot 2 vs. Spring Boot 3, and JDK 8 vs. JDK 11+ versions for JSQLParser).
   • Consider color coding different kinds of modules (for example, one color for core modules, another for extension/plugins, another for integration modules, and another for testing/samples).

6. Key Elements to Include in the Diagram:
   • Each major module (as mentioned above) should be a clearly labeled box.
   • Arrows should show dependency directions (e.g., “Mybatis-Plus Generator” → “Mybatis-Plus Core” or “Spring Auto-Configuration” → “Mybatis-Plus Extension/ Core”).
   • Use legend symbols (such as shapes or colors) to distinguish between libraries, interfaces, configuration modules, and testing code.
   • If desired, include annotations to denote design patterns (like “Plugin”, “Active Record”, or “Auto-configuration”) near the relevant modules.
   • Optional: a layer breakdown that shows “Framework Core”, “Extensions/Pluggable Modules”, and “Integration/Starter Modules”.

By following these instructions, you will create a detailed and accurate system design diagram that explains how MyBatis-Plus as a framework is architected. This diagram will not only be useful for communicating the high-level modular architecture to team members and stakeholders but also serves as a guide to understand the intricate relationships between the various components of this powerful project.
</explanation>
